subject: Follow-up: Technical deep-dive (60-90m) — scheduling & agenda asks
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@lumosai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Technical deep-dive (60-90m) — scheduling & agenda asks

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the discovery call earlier. Quick recap and next steps:

Recap (1-liner): Lumos.ai is exploring low-latency, multi-tenant inference for a customer-facing search assistant (target: 50–200 qps, 3–5s p95 today, interested in lowering cost while holding quality).

Proposed next step: 60–90 minute technical deep dive with our ML/Infra engineers to align on architecture, throughput requirements, and a short ops checklist we can run together. Goal: leave the call with a proposed capacity profile and a rough rollout plan.

Suggested windows (Pacific):
- Tue Apr 20: 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed Apr 21: 09:00–10:30 or 15:00–16:30

Pre-call asks (to help Marissa/Dylan prep):
- Representative request profile (avg tokens per request, typical prompt length)
- Expected concurrency and peak windows (e.g., regional spikes)
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, retention)
- Sample payloads or anonymized logs if available (we treat this as confidential)

Attachments: discovery notes (PDF) and a short TDX prep checklist.

If those windows don't work, here is a short poll link to suggest alternatives: https://calendar.redwood.com/poll/8f3d2a

Thanks — if you confirm a slot I’ll send calendar invites (60/90min) with a draft agenda.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@lumosai.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Technical deep-dive (60-90m) — scheduling & agenda asks

Thanks, Mateo — appreciated the summary and the checklist. Jordan and I discussed and the Tue Apr 20 14:00–15:30 PT window works for us. Please calendar it as 90 minutes — we want to include a short engineering lead Q&A and a security question set.

Quick answers to pre-call asks:
- Avg tokens per request: ~120 tokens; peak prompts (with context): up to 450 tokens
- Expected concurrency: 60 avg, with short peaks to ~220 for new feature launches
- Data residency: must keep EU customer data in EU region; otherwise US-hosted is fine
- We can share anonymized logs after an NDA; Jordan will send preferred format.

Jordan (cc): could you share a short doc with current infra (VM sizes, current model variants) so Marissa has a heads-up?

See you Tuesday — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, Lumos AI
alicia.gomez@lumosai.com | +1 617-555-0191

Thanks Mateo — slot confirmed on our side for Tue 14:00–15:30 PT (90m). Looping in a short draft agenda and prep items so everyone arrives aligned.

Draft agenda (90m):
1) 14:00–14:05 — quick intros & success criteria (Mateo / Alicia)
2) 14:05–14:25 — Lumos current infra & workload profile (Jordan)
3) 14:25–14:50 — Redwood architecture options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (Marissa)
4) 14:50–15:10 — Throughput/latency sizing exercise + cost tradeoffs (Marissa/Dylan)
5) 15:10–15:25 — Security/compliance & data residency callouts (Marissa)
6) 15:25–15:30 — Next steps & action items (Mateo)

Prep asks for Lumos (Jordan/Alicia):
- Example request traces (anonymized) or sizes by percentile (p50/p95)
- A one-paragraph non-sensitive description of the launch timeline (helps prioritization)
- Any regulatory controls beyond EU residency (encryption at rest, audit logs)

Engineering notes for Dylan/Marissa:
- If Lumos expects bursts to ~220 concurrency we should plan a fallback routing policy (smaller cheaper variants + autoscale headroom).
- Bring quantization/latency runbook and sample perf numbers for a 13B/70B family we typically recommend.
- Prepare a short checklist for preflight (network egress, VPC peering, KMS integration).

Attachments: TDX prep checklist (tdx-prep-checklist.md) and a blank runbook template (attached as stub).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
